correctness.rationale: All terms have positive real conductances and the well-defined zero-target discrete-time Kemeny invariant. The commute time identity and exact two-arc parallel resistance yield formula (3); an explicit endpoint/interior partition proves the all-n one-edge factorization. Ten rational C5 pair contributions yield exact negative change at fixed total weight. Strict Jensen gives the unique C3 equality, and the bipartite block determinant gives exactly the C4 equality family. A positive one-coordinate second variation and negative budget direction prove saddle, not global optimality. The independent Fraction-based hitting-time verifier passed 631 tests; finite evidence supplements the algebraic all-real/all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2012 primary paper optimizes graph topology/spectra without a fixed weighted-cycle conductance-design theorem. The 2016 tree paper treats graph-edge insertion, with inaccessible later full text noted. Full publicly available result texts on cycle-chord Kemeny, weighted-cycle cover fairness, and priced-five-cycle continuous-time spectral gaps have different dynamics/objects and do not contain or imply the simultaneous new coordinatewise trap, five-site descent, and sharp three/four-site exclusion. No matching indexed statement was identified; unindexed historic equivalent work is a real residual originality risk.
residual_risks: The complete 2016 Kirkland--Zeng publisher paper was not accessible here; abstract/intro and its tree-focused descriptions do not exclude every implicit cycle corollary.
Older specialist treatments of conductance-sensitive Kemeny optimization may be unindexed or may imply the simple exact counterexample without matching its title.
The proposed result is not a complete global optimizer classification for five cycles or larger; neither proof nor originality claim extends that far.

value.rationale: Kemeny is a natural global stationary-target travel-time cost, and edge weights are directly controlled under a conductance budget. The theorem identifies the smallest simple cycle where optimizing or testing every single edge separately is misleading: each coordinate has a strict optimum but a feasible coordinated direction strictly improves the real objective. A sharp C3/C4 boundary and universal single-edge formula establish mathematical structure beyond one arbitrary sample, without claiming large practical gains or global optimal five-cycle values.
